source: USDA Food and Nutrition Service, Thrifty Food Plan, 2021 (report FNS-916, August 2021), table 'Thrifty Food Plan Market Basket for the reference family of four, June 2021: aggregate quantities, costs, and cost shares of Market Basket Categories in weekly amounts', report pages 37-38. https://fns-prod.azureedge.us/sites/default/files/resource-files/TFP2021.pdf
household: reference family of four: a man and a woman age 20-50, a child age 6-8, and a child age 9-11
units: weekly quantities in pounds, as purchased; cost in June 2021 dollars

grain_wg_staple.label: Whole-grain staple grains (e.g., rice, pasta, breads, tortillas)

grain_rg_staple.label: Refined-grain staple grains (e.g., rice, pasta, breads, tortillas)

dairy_lowfat.label: Low- and non-fat milk, yogurt, soy alternatives

dairy_higherfat.label: Higher fat milk, yogurt, soy alternatives

misc_prepared.label: Pre-prepared entrees and side dishes (e.g., soups, frozen entrees, pizza)

misc_sauces_sugars.label: Sauces, condiments, jams, honey, sugars, spices

misc_other.label: Other foods and beverages (e.g., soft drinks, fruit drinks, ice cream, pudding, cookies, candy bars)

quotes.milk_fl_oz: For some Market Basket Categories (e.g., low- and non-fat milk, yogurt, and soy alternatives), the amount in pounds can be converted to an approximate amount in fluid ounces by multiplying by 15.34. (table footnote c)
quotes.coffee: the Market Baskets for adults ages 20 and older contain a minimum of 1 cup per day of coffee or tea. (Methods, practicality constraints)
quotes.beans_canned: In the Thrifty Food Plan, 2021 nearly all (99 percent) are assumed to be purchased as canned varieties. (Results)
